text:
Leaving Tokyo at noon for Kamakura? The temples in Hase stop letting people in around 16:30, and in winter that's almost exactly when the sun goes down over the sea. Plan it in that order and the day takes care of itself 👇

🎯 Guess first: which big Kamakura sight is still open at 8 p.m.? The answer's here 👉 https://japanbystation.com/kamakura-from-noon-temples-or-sunset

We built this afternoon from the temples' and the railway's own pages, and checked every time and fare before putting it up.

🚆 GETTING THERE

The 11:36 Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station reaches Kamakura at 12:33 with no change. That's ¥1,040 by ticket or ¥1,034 by IC card, and the JR Pass covers it.

1️⃣ TEMPLES FIRST

Take the little green Enoden two stops to Hase (¥200). The Great Buddha lets people in until 16:45 in winter, and Hasedera, five minutes away, takes last entry at 16:30. Have a late lunch at the temple's own restaurant, looking out over Yuigahama beach.

2️⃣ THEN THE SUNSET

Two more stops to Inamuragasaki and an 8-minute walk to the cape. The view runs along Shichirigahama to Enoshima, and on windy days from December to February, Mount Fuji often joins in.

3️⃣ THEN THE SHRINE

Back to Kamakura (¥220) and 10 minutes on foot to Tsurugaoka Hachimangu, whose gates stay open until 20:00 every day.

🌅 OUR TAKE

Don't try to squeeze in Kita-Kamakura as well. One area, three short train rides and a sunset make a much better afternoon than six temples at a jog. In summer the sun sets around 19:00, so there's time for the beach too.
